description: Graph app integration — LinguaScrape consumes the shared culture-scrape graph: a Neo4j TypeScript driver layer for relational queries plus a FastAPI proxy for search and Datalog inference, surfaced through the existing UnifiedExplorer adapter system, entity graph views, provenance UI, and federated search, degrading gracefully when the graph is offline.

tasks.title: T16-US-001: Sidecar + Neo4j dev orchestration & configuration
tasks.description:
As a developer, I need to run culture-scrape (FastAPI) and Neo4j alongside LinguaScrape so the app can query the shared graph in dev and prod.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Add docker-compose services: culturescrape (`culturescrape serve`, default port 8800) and neo4j (with a profile), plus a documented dev script
- Add and document env vars: CULTURESCRAPE_API_URL, CULTURESCRAPE_ENABLED, NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD in .env and .env.example
- Add an npm script `dev:full` that starts the LinguaScrape server, the sidecar, and Neo4j together
- Both the FastAPI health endpoint and the Neo4j bolt port are reachable from the server process in dev
- Type checks pass (`npm run check`)

Project context: LinguaScrape is a TypeScript/React/Vite + Express app with TSV-first storage (lexicons/*.tsv, 57 files), served by server/index.ts + server/routes.ts, client in client/src. culture-scrape (vendored in-repo at packages/culture-scrape/) is a Python CLI/FastAPI engine that emits a canonical node/edge graph and exports to Neo4j + Datalog. The agreed data-layer target is a SHARED CANONICAL SCHEMA with Neo4j/Datalog as the correlation system-of-record; TSV stays the portable source of truth; the app backend stays TypeScript (no Python rewrite). The authoritative design is docs/culturescrape-integration.md. Acceptance uses TypeScript checks: `npm run check` (tsc) and vitest (network/graph calls mocked against fixtures — no live sidecar/Neo4j in tests). This story belongs to tasklist 16 (Graph app integration — LinguaScrape consumes the shared culture-scrape graph: a Neo4j TypeScript driver layer for relational queries plus a FastAPI proxy for search and Datalog inference, surfaced through the existing UnifiedExplorer adapter system, entity graph views, provenance UI, and federated search, degrading gracefully when the graph is offline.). NOTE: culture-scrape is vendored in this same repo at packages/culture-scrape/, so the Python-side ingestion/reconciliation/Datalog work is an in-repo concern (ralphy can modify packages/culture-scrape/ directly) — see its own tasklists under packages/culture-scrape/ralph/. This tasklist covers the shared schema + the TypeScript app side.

tasks.title: T16-US-002: Neo4j TypeScript data-access layer
tasks.description:

- Create server/services/graph-store.ts using the official neo4j-driver: parameterized Cypher for node lookup, neighborhood traversal (depth 1-3), and correlation queries
- Export typed GraphNode/GraphEdge/Neighborhood results validated at the boundary; connection pooling + timeouts configured from env
- isAvailable() health check with short-lived caching; safe teardown on shutdown
- vitest unit tests run against a mocked driver (no live Neo4j) covering success, timeout, and unavailable paths
- Type checks pass (`npm run check`)

tasks.title: T16-US-004: First-party graph API routes
tasks.description:

- Add routes in server/routes.ts: GET /api/graph/search, GET /api/graph/node/:id, GET /api/graph/neighborhood/:id?depth=, GET /api/graph/metrics, GET /api/graph/status
- Node/neighborhood routes use graph-store.ts (Neo4j); search/metrics use culturescrape-client.ts
- When the graph/sidecar is unavailable, routes return HTTP 503 with a structured { available:false } body and never crash
- Integration tests (vitest) exercise each route with graph-store and client mocked, including the unavailable path
- Routes documented in docs/culturescrape-integration.md

tasks.title: T16-US-005: Health monitoring & graceful degradation
tasks.description:
As a user, I want the app to work normally when the graph is offline, with graph features clearly disabled rather than broken.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- A health service polls/caches availability of both Neo4j and the FastAPI sidecar; /api/graph/status reflects them
- A client hook/context (useGraphAvailability) exposes availability to components
- Graph-dependent UI (buttons, tabs, the explorer adapter) is hidden or disabled with an explanatory tooltip when unavailable
- Tests cover up->down->up transitions and confirm non-graph features are unaffected
- No unhandled promise rejections or console errors when the graph is down

tasks.title: T16-US-006: Entity ID resolution at query time
tasks.description:

- Ambiguous matches are logged with confidence and never silently mis-linked
- vitest tests cover alias-hit, fuzzy fallback, and no-match cases on fixtures
- Type checks pass (`npm run check`)
